analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation and comment text only. The ProviderConfig.swift patch (hunk at ~line 156) edits a doc comment to say that models on the native `auto` paged allowlist start at concurrency 8 on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra. It changes no executable code. docs/reference/configuration.md was supplied only as head text with no diff, so I could not tell which lines changed and read it as a whole.

What the head text states:
- It is consistent with T-041. The SSD prefix-cache TTL is capped at 1800s, `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE` is the single gate, and there are no new at-rest fields.
- Endpoint resumption adds no env var or config key, creates no local trust and extends no proof lifetime. This is consistent with TB-011/T-053.
- The App Attest worker opt-in is exact `1`, forwarded only for the worker flag, and not production-ready. Fallback to in-process Apple calls is not allowed, which is consistent with T-052/T-053.
- `darkbloom logout` takes its issuer from metadata bound to the token (A-008). With no metadata it logs out locally only, with a warning.
- The TB-010 fan-helper and TB-002 wire contracts are untouched.

The documented concurrency default of 8 raises only an availability and memory load question (T-010/T-029). Admission checks, thermal and Low Power Mode downgrade, and physical-memory limits are said to remain. I did not verify the code behind that claim, because ServingPerformanceProfiles was not supplied. The next pass should confirm the comment matches that code if it is in scope.

I found no security regression, new attack surface, or invalidated threat assumption in these units.
